title: Motivic Hall Algebras and Integration Maps

items.title: Relative motivic stack-function groups for quiver representation stacks

references.title: Dominic Joyce, Configurations in abelian categories. II. Ringel-Hall algebras, arXiv:math/0503029v2, §§2–3
Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §§2.1–3.5

items.statement:
Fix a field $k$. An Artin $k$-stack is as in
[[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]]. In this item, a finite-type stack means an
Artin $k$-stack with a finite-type smooth atlas and finite-type diagonal. It
has affine stabilizers when the automorphism group scheme of every geometric
point is affine.

For a finite-type Artin stack $X$ with affine stabilizers, define
$\mathscr K(X)$ to be the abelian group generated by isomorphism classes
$[Y\to X]$ of finite-type Artin stacks $Y$ with affine stabilizers and a
1-morphism to $X$. Impose the following relations.

1. If $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed substack, then
   $[Y\to X]=[Z\to X]+[Y\setminus Z\to X]$.
2. Let $S\to X$ be a finite-type stack and let
   $d:V_0\to V_1$ be a constant-rank morphism of vector bundles on $S$.
   The additive vector bundle $V_0$ acts on $V_1$ by translation through
   $d$. Write $[V_1/V_0\to S\to X]$ for the resulting quotient groupoid
   stack over $X$. If $r_i$ is the rank of $V_i$, impose
   $[V_1/V_0\to X]=\mathbb L^{r_1-r_0}[S\to X]$.

Here $\mathbb L$ is the class of $\mathbb A^1_k$ in
$R:=\mathscr K(\operatorname{Spec}k)$, and we localize $R$ and the modules
$\mathscr K(X)$ by making $\mathbb L$ invertible. The product in $R$ is
induced by product over $k$. The group $\mathscr K(X)$ is an $R$-module.
This explicit vector-bundle-stack relation records the class of a family of
linear objects modulo its linear changes of splitting.

For a morphism $f:X\to X'$, pullback is
$f^*[Y\to X']=[Y\times_{X'}X\to X]$ and pushforward is
$f_![Z\to X]=[Z\to X\to X']$. Exterior product is
$[Y\to X]\boxtimes[Z\to X']=[Y\times_k Z\to X\times_kX']$.
These operations are well-defined because fiber product and composition
preserve isomorphisms, closed-substack decompositions, and the
vector-bundle-stack relation. If the rank of a vector-bundle map varies, its
base is partitioned into the finitely many locally closed rank strata and
the scissor relation is applied on those strata.

The dependency on [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the cited
algebraic-stack convention in [[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]], specifically
its represented-sheaf descent foundation. No choice is used in the
finite-dimensional quiver matrix calculations below.

items.title: Derived and cohomological Hall algebras are distinct constructions

references.title: Bertrand Toën, Derived Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0501343v4, §§3–4
Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson–Thomas invariants, arXiv:1006.2706v2, §§2 and 8

items.statement:
The present page uses the ordinary finite-quiver representation stacks and
relative Grothendieck stack-function classes of
[[def-motivic-hall-algebra-of-a-finite-quiver]]. Toën's derived Hall
construction is defined on the core homotopy type of perfect modules over a
locally finite dg-enhancement over a finite field
([[def-toen-derived-hall-algebra]],
[[def-toen-locally-finite-dg-category]]). Its arrows are weighted by homotopy
cardinality after fixing source and homotopy cofiber; the locally finite
homotopy-type definition specifies the finite higher-homotopy weights
([[def-locally-finite-homotopy-type]]). This is a different coefficient
carrier from Grothendieck classes of ordinary representation stacks.

The untwisted quiver CoHA uses rational equivariant
Borel–Moore homology of representation spaces and the exact-sequence
correspondence ([[def-untwisted-quiver-cohomological-hall-algebra]],
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]).
Its convention is subrepresentation first and quotient second. It uses the intrinsic quotient-stack grading
$\mathbb H_i([X/G])=H_{i+2\dim G}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X)$ of
[[def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore-grading]], rather than the variety grading of the published fixed-group definition. Its
homological shift is $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$ for subdimension $\mathbf a$
and quotient dimension $\mathbf b$. The CoHA definition constructs that product through the locally proved parabolic/Levi quotient-stack operation package; its intrinsic shift must not be assigned to the raw variety-normalized groups. For a quiver potential, the critical construction retains monodromy and uses coherent homological coefficients
([[def-quiver-potential-and-monodromic-vanishing-cycle-data]],
[[def-critical-quiver-coha-from-vanishing-cycle-data]]). The standard rational vanishing-cycle instance is constructed in
[[lem-standard-rational-quiver-vanishing-cycles-realize-critical-correspondences]], using the quotient-stack maps of
[[thm-quiver-quotient-stack-borel-moore-operation-package]]. Its coefficient is the variety-normalized dual shifted by $-2\dim G$, so the same intrinsic Euler-form degree applies. This does not assert a mixed Hodge enrichment or a general 3-Calabi–Yau orientation-data theorem.

These constructions have different carriers, coefficient theories, and
conventions; a shared extension pattern does not identify their algebras. No
comparison map between them, orientation-dependent 3-Calabi–Yau integration
theorem, or physical BPS state identification is claimed here.

items.title: The motivic Hall algebra of a finite quiver

references.title: Dominic Joyce, Configurations in abelian categories. II. Ringel-Hall algebras, arXiv:math/0503029v2, §5.1
Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §§4.1–4.2

items.statement:
Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver over a field $k$. A representation
of $Q$ assigns a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V_i$ to each vertex
$i\in Q_0$ and a linear map $V_{s(a)}\to V_{t(a)}$ to each arrow
$a\in Q_1$. Its dimension vector is
$\mathbf d=(\dim V_i)_{i\in Q_0}\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$.

For $\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ put
$$\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}(Q) =\prod_{a\in Q_1}\operatorname{Hom}_k (k^{d_{s(a)}},k^{d_{t(a)}}),\qquad G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}_{d_i}(k),$$and let $\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)=[\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}(Q)/ G_{\mathbf d}]$ be the quotient Artin stack. It is finite type and has affine stabilizers: the representation variety and the acting group are finite type and affine, and each stabilizer is a closed subgroup of $G_{\mathbf d}$. For dimension vectors $\mathbf d,\mathbf e$, let $\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}(Q)$ be the stack of short exact sequences of representations$$0\longrightarrow B_{\mathbf e}\longrightarrow E_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e} \longrightarrow A_{\mathbf d}\longrightarrow0.$$The endpoints are part of the data, and isomorphisms are isomorphisms of the whole exact sequence. Equivalently, after choosing the standard $\mathbf e$-dimensional subspaces at each vertex, this is the quotient by the product parabolic preserving those subspaces of the affine space of block upper-triangular arrow maps. Thus $\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}(Q)$ is a finite-type Artin stack with affine stabilizers. More explicitly, on a local splitting $E_i=B_i\oplus A_i$, the arrow $a:i\to j$ has block matrix$$\begin{pmatrix} B_a & \xi_a\\ 0 & A_a \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \xi_a:A_i\to B_j.$$Changing the splitting by $h_i:A_i\to B_i$ changes $\xi_a$ to $\xi_a+B_a h_i-h_j A_a$. This is the translation action of the vector bundle $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,B_i)$ on $\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,B_j)$ used in the extension stack calculation. Let $q:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}$ send a sequence to its quotient, $s:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}\to \mathfrak M_{\mathbf e}$ send it to its subrepresentation, and $m:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}$ send it to its middle representation. The Hall correspondence is ~~~ tikzcd & \mathfrak E_{\mathbf d,\mathbf e}(Q) \ar[dl,"(q,s)"'] \ar[dr,"m"] & \\ \mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf e}(Q) && \mathfrak M_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}(Q) ~~~ Its arrows record the ordered quotient, subrepresentation, and middle object of the displayed short exact sequence; the diagram fixes the convolution convention. Define$$H_Q:=\bigoplus_{\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}} \mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)).$$For $\alpha\in\mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d})$ and $\beta\in\mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf e})$, define$$\alpha*\beta :=m_!\big((q,s)^*(\alpha\boxtimes\beta)\big) \in\mathscr K(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}).$$
Thus the first factor is the quotient and the second factor is the
subrepresentation, so the sequence is
$0\to B\to E\to A\to0$. Each homogeneous product is defined by one
finite-type stack correspondence; no completion or finiteness of a sum over
isomorphism classes is required. This is the stack-function product without
a potential or a vanishing-cycle weight.

items.title: Finite-field groupoid cardinality for quiver stack specializations

references.title: Dominic Joyce, Configurations in abelian categories. II. Ringel-Hall algebras, arXiv:math/0503029v2, §§2–3
Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §§2–3

items.statement:
Let $k=\mathbb F_q$. A finite groupoid is a groupoid with finitely many
isomorphism classes of objects and finite automorphism groups. Its
**groupoid cardinality** is
$$|\mathcal G|=\sum_{[x]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal G)} \frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal G}(x)|}.$$
For a quotient stack in the finite-quiver construction whose rational-point
groupoid is finite, define its point-count value by the groupoid cardinality
of that rational-point groupoid. This definition applies, in particular, to
$\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)$, the exact-sequence stacks, and the
vector-bundle-stack fibers in the examples below. Its compatibility with the
relations defining $\mathscr K$ is established by
[[lem-finite-field-stack-groupoid-cardinality-respects-motivic-relations]].

items.title: The motive of a quiver extension stack

references.title: Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §4.1 and §7.1
Dominic Joyce, Configurations in abelian categories. II. Ringel-Hall algebras, arXiv:math/0503029v2, §§4–5

items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite quiver over $k$, and let $X\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)$ and
$Y\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf e}(Q)$ be finite-type stack families of quotient
representations $A$ and subrepresentations $B$. Let
$\mathfrak E_{X,Y}$ be the stack of exact sequences
$0\to B\to E\to A\to0$ with the endpoint identifications supplied by $X$
and $Y$. Define the bilinear Euler form
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e) =\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a\in Q_1}d_{s(a)}e_{t(a)}.$$Then the relative motivic class over $X\times Y$ is$$[\mathfrak E_{X,Y}\to X\times Y] =\mathbb L^{-\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)} [X\times Y\to X\times Y]$$
in the vector-bundle-stack coefficient theory of
[[def-motivic-stack-function-groups-for-quiver-representations]]. The
statement concerns extension groupoids, so automorphisms of an extension
that act trivially on its two endpoints are retained.
items.strategy: Represent extensions by off-diagonal arrow maps modulo changes of splitting and apply the vector-stack relation on finite rank strata.

items.title: Quiver motivic Hall convolution is associative and unital

references.title: Dominic Joyce, Configurations in abelian categories. II. Ringel-Hall algebras, arXiv:math/0503029v2, §5.1, Theorem 5.2
Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §4.2, Theorem 4.3

items.statement:
For a finite quiver $Q$ over $k$, the convolution in
[[def-motivic-hall-algebra-of-a-finite-quiver]] is an associative unital
$R$-bilinear product on $H_Q$. Its unit is the class of the zero-representation
stack in degree $\mathbf 0$.
items.strategy: Identify both parenthesizations with the same stack of three-step flags and use functoriality of pullback and pushforward.

items.title: The Euler-twisted dimension-vector algebra of a quiver

references.title: Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §§4.3 and 5.2
Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §§1.2–1.3

items.statement:
For a finite quiver $Q$, let $R$ and the invertible class $\mathbb L$ be
as in [[def-motivic-stack-function-groups-for-quiver-representations]].
For dimension vectors $\mathbf d,\mathbf e\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ define
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e) =\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i- \sum_{a\in Q_1}d_{s(a)}e_{t(a)}.$$This is the Euler pairing for the fixed quiver representation convention: the first argument is the quotient dimension and the second is the subrepresentation dimension. It is bilinear by its displayed finite-sum formula. Let $T_Q=\bigoplus_{\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}}R\,x^{\mathbf d}$ be the free $R$-module on formal symbols $x^{\mathbf d}$. Equip it with the bilinear multiplication$$x^{\mathbf d}x^{\mathbf e} =\mathbb L^{-\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)} x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}.$$
The subsequent theorem verifies associativity and the unit $x^{\mathbf 0}$.
This is the Euler-twisted dimension-vector monoid algebra used as the
target of the stack integration map; the formula fixes its twist convention.

items.title: Finite-field groupoid cardinality respects the motivic stack relations

references.title: Dominic Joyce, Configurations in abelian categories. II. Ringel-Hall algebras, arXiv:math/0503029v2, §§2–3
Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §3

items.statement:
For the finite-quiver quotient stacks over $\mathbb F_q$ whose rational-point
groupoids are finite, groupoid cardinality is additive under closed/open
decomposition and multiplicative under product. It respects the
vector-bundle-stack relation
$$[V_1/V_0\to S] =\mathbb L^{r_1-r_0}[S\to S],$$
so it defines a ring realization on the subring of motivic classes generated
by these stacks, and it sends $\mathbb L$ to $q$.
items.strategy: Compute action-groupoid cardinality orbit by orbit and check the vector-stack relation over each finite stratum.

items.title: Motivic stack Hall and untwisted finitary Hall have different carriers

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §§1.1–1.3
Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §§4.1–4.2

items.statement:
The actual current PA-19 Definition was inspected as the upstream interface;
it remains a draft carrier in its owning pair until ordinary readiness and
review. This item uses only its stated coefficient carrier and product
formula.
items.strategy: Compare the two declared carriers and coefficient operations directly; make no unstated comparison map.

items.title: Quiver stack integration is multiplicative with the Euler twist

references.title: Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §5.2 and §§7.1–7.2
Dominic Joyce, Configurations in abelian categories. II. Ringel-Hall algebras, arXiv:math/0503029v2, §6.2, Theorem 6.4 and proof

items.statement:
For a finite quiver $Q$ over $k$, equip $T_Q$ with the multiplication in
[[def-quiver-motivic-quantum-torus]]. The product is associative and has
unit $x^{\mathbf0}$. Define
$$\mathcal I_Q:H_Q\to T_Q,\qquad \mathcal I_Q([X\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}(Q)]) =[X]\,x^{\mathbf d}.$$
Then $\mathcal I_Q$ is a well-defined $R$-algebra homomorphism. The exact
twist is $\mathbb L^{-\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)}$ for the product of a
quotient of dimension $\mathbf d$ and a subrepresentation of dimension
$\mathbf e$. This result uses the stack of ordinary representations of $Q$
with no potential and no vanishing-cycle weight. It makes no claim about an
orientation-dependent 3-Calabi–Yau or Donaldson–Thomas integration map.
items.strategy: Use bilinearity for target associativity and the extension-stack motive for multiplicativity on generators.

title: Motivic Hall Algebras and Integration Maps: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The motivic Hall product for a one-vertex zero-arrow quiver

references.title: Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §§4.1–4.2 and 5.2
Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §§1.1–1.3

items.statement:
Let $Q$ have one vertex and no arrows.

~~~tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}
\node[circle,draw,inner sep=1.5pt,label=below:{1}] (v) at (0,0) {};
\end{tikzpicture}
~~~

The vertex label is $1$; the absence of edges means a representation is
only a finite-dimensional vector space. Let $S$ be its one-dimensional
representation and let $\delta_S=[B\operatorname{GL}_1\to
\mathfrak M_1(Q)]$ be the identity stack function. For every field $k$,
$$\mathcal I_Q(\delta_S*\delta_S) =\mathbb L^{-1}[B\operatorname{GL}_1]^2x^2.$$
On the finite-field groupoid-count specialization $k=\mathbb F_q$, this
coefficient is $q^{-1}(q-1)^{-2}$.
items.strategy: Compute the endpoint and extension groupoids and multiply their finite groupoid cardinalities.

items.title: An untwisted monoid map fails for the one-arrow quiver

references.title: Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, arXiv:1002.4372v1, §5.2
Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §§1.1–1.3

items.statement:
The claim that stack integration always maps quiver motivic Hall products
multiplicatively to the untwisted dimension-vector monoid algebra is false.
Here “untwisted” means the target rule
$x^{\mathbf d}x^{\mathbf e}=x^{\mathbf d+\mathbf e}$, while the source map
is $\mathcal I_Q([X\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}])=[X]x^{\mathbf d}$.

Let $Q$ have vertices $1,2$ and one arrow $1\to2$.

~~~tikzcd
1 \arrow[r] & 2
~~~

For $k=\mathbb F_2$, let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be the representations supported
at vertices $1$ and $2$. Use $S_1$ as quotient and $S_2$ as subrepresentation.
There are two exact sequences with these fixed endpoints, distinguished by
the arrow map of the middle representation. The stack groupoid count of
$\delta_{S_1}*\delta_{S_2}$ is $2$, whereas the product of the two integrated
classes in the untwisted target has coefficient $1$.
items.strategy: Enumerate the two off-diagonal arrow maps over F2 and compare source and target coefficients.
